title: Staff per department
prompt: Show each department_id and its number of employees, as staff. Replace the ___.
hints: Group by the column you're summarising by.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees;
wrongSolutions.why: Without GROUP BY, there's one row

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS staff FROM employees GROUP BY id;

title: Products per category
prompt: Show each category, its number of products as products, and its average price as average_price.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS products, AVG(price) AS average_price FROM products GROUP BY category;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS products, AVG(cost) AS average_price FROM products GROUP BY category;
SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS products FROM products GROUP BY category;

title: Grouped by two columns
prompt: Show each combination of customer_id and status, with its number of orders as orders.
hints: List both columns in GROUP BY.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (14, 7, '2024-04-01', 'shipped');

solutions: SELECT customer_id, status, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id, status;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT customer_id, status, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;
SELECT customer_id, status, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY status;

title: City averages
prompt: Show each city and its average temperature rounded to 1 decimal, as avg_temp, sorted by city.
solutions: SELECT city, ROUND(AVG(temp_c), 1) AS avg_temp FROM readings GROUP BY city ORDER BY city;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, ROUND(AVG(temp_c), 1) AS avg_temp FROM readings GROUP BY reading_date ORDER BY city;
SELECT city, ROUND(MAX(temp_c), 1) AS avg_temp FROM readings GROUP BY city ORDER BY city;

title: The NULL group
prompt: Show each manager_id and the number of employees reporting to it, as reports. Employees with no manager form their own NULL row.
hints: GROUP BY keeps NULL as a group.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT manager_id, COUNT(*) AS reports FROM employees GROUP BY manager_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT manager_id, COUNT(*) AS reports FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY manager_id;
SELECT manager_id, COUNT(manager_id) AS reports FROM employees GROUP BY manager_id;

cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (14, 7, '2024-04-01', 'pending');

title: Monthly orders
prompt: Show each month like 2024-01 as month, and its number of orders as orders, in date order.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY order_date ORDER BY month;
SELECT strftime('%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

title: Item revenue
prompt: Show each order_id and its total units multiplied by 2 as value, highest value first. Break ties by order_id.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * 2) AS value FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id ORDER BY value DESC, order_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS value FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id ORDER BY value DESC, order_id;
SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * 2) AS value FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id ORDER BY value, order_id;
